scenes.heading: Choosing and maintaining your camera gear kit

sents.d: Choosing and maintaining your camera gear kit
Reliability matters more than owning the newest equipment.

A dependable starting kit usually includes one primary camera body, a backup body or at minimum a backup camera option, two or three lenses covering your typical shooting distances, and enough memory cards and batteries for a full day without needing to stop and offload.
Testing gear before a paid shoot — not during one — catches problems like a failing battery or a corrupted card while there's still time to fix them.
A gear insurance policy is worth the relatively small annual cost once your kit represents a meaningful investment, since a single theft or accident could otherwise end your ability to work.

take: Carry backups, test before shoots, and insure your gear.
